text:
olga: Heads-up — bringing up a compact embedding variant 'crane-lite-v2-384' for onboarding. Quick sanity checks show odd behavior for very short queries (<=3 tokens). anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: saw something similar with another compact model last quarter. can you paste the recall@k vs query length? :thinking_face:

olga: sure, ran a quick sweep on NQ/dev + our internal kb. commands: ```python run_eval.py --model crane-lite-v2-384 --dataset nq_dev --group-by query_len --metrics recall@1,5,10,cosine_gap``` output: 
len<=3: r@10 0.42
len4-10: r@10 0.78
len>10: r@10 0.81
Also noticed embedding norms for short queries are ~0.6x the usual.

maya: embedding norm drop is interesting — could be tokenizer truncation or special-token effect. which tokenizer/config used?

olga: using shared tokenizer from crane-base, same bpe. no hard truncation. added debug print: tokens for "what" -> ["what"] (ok), for very short q sometimes returns leading whitespace token? unlikely.

lee: can you run cosine vs dot product comparison? if norms shrink cosine may be stable but dot will drop.

olga: good call. quick table: 
len<=3: cosine@10 0.80, dot@10 0.42
len4-10: cosine@10 0.79, dot@10 0.78
so cosine stays consistent. norm scaling seems the culprit.

sarah: sounds like a linear-scaling bias in output head when input length small. maybe final layer norm not seeing enough context so scale bias is lower. any quantization on this model?

olga: model shipped with per-tensor 6-bit quant from our fast-quant pipeline. i also evaluated a float32 variant and saw similar norm shrink but slightly less severe (0.75 vs 0.6).

raj: okay two axes: (1) tokenizer / input preprocessing (2) model-level bias on short contexts. try augmenting short queries with a lightweight sentinel token during eval, e.g., prefix with "Q: ".

olga: quick experiment: prefixed "Q: " to queries <=3 -> norms back to ~0.95 and r@10 rises to 0.76. interesting.

maya: that indicates the model expects some minimal context distribution. maybe during pretraining short queries were rare or had prefixes. we should add a small calibration hook in production: for queries <4, add prefix "Q:" by default. but we need to verify downstream effects (false positives).

lee: also run clustering purity for short-query subsets. if clustering collapses it could affect rerank too.

olga: ran HDBSCAN on a 5k short-query sample from prod-like logs: purity dropped by ~12% vs baseline. with prefixing, purity recovered ~9% but some clusters merged differently.

raj: actionable plan: 1) Add short-query prefixing as an opt-in calibration in the SDK. 2) Add a unit eval in the onboarding harness to run query-length stratified metrics. 3) File an issue to check pretraining sample distribution for short inputs.

olga: I'll open the PR for SDK opt-in flag + add eval. dropping notes into the onboarding checklist.

eval-bot: test-run summary attached: "crane-lite-v2-384 / nq_dev / stratified" -> baseline r@10 0.42 (<=3), with-prefix r@10 0.76, overall r@10 0.80. CI run id: ci-648992.

sarah: awesome. after PR, let's roll a canary to dedicated with prefixing to measure customer impact. also add a comment to model card about short-query calibration. :memo:

olga: thanks team. tagging @maya for model-card blurb and @lee to add the stratified test in the harness. will follow up with PR link. :thumbsup:
